newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end higher on Menem hopes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end higher on Menem hopes.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose Friday on short-covering on expectations that President Carlos Menem will unveil policies to liberalize the labor market.

"There are many expectations about what Menem is going to say," said a proprietary analyst at a large foreign bank, referring to Menem's anticipated speech at an industrialist conference Friday evening.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose 0.40 to 115.20 while Argentina's FRB due 2005 advanced1/8 to $77-5/8.
The longer it takes to pass the measure, the more fragile sentiment could become. "In the meantime it does a lot of damage to confidence," said an analyst at a large Argentine bank.

Apart from watching out for concrete signs that the government's economic measures will get smooth passage through Congress, players will be keeping an eye on the U.S. next week with the important August jobs report due for release on Friday.
In addition, the Labor Day holiday in the U.S. on Monday could keep a lid on activity in Argentina at the beginning of the week.
Traders reported thin volumes this session.
